public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hilbert's Fifth Problem and the Hilbert–Smith Conjecture

The **Hilbert–Smith conjecture** states that a locally compact topological group acting
continuously and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold must be a
Lie group. It remains open in general; Pardon proved it for 3-manifolds in 2013.
An equivalent formulation: no p-adic integer group `ℤ_[p]` can act faithfully on any
connected finite-dimensional topological manifold.

## Main statements

- `hilbert_smith_conjecture`: the Hilbert–Smith conjecture.
- `hilbert_smith_padic_formulation`: the equivalent formulation for `ℤ_[p]`.
- `hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three`: Pardon's theorem for 3-manifolds.
- `hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian`: the case of isometric actions on Riemannian
  manifolds.
- `hilbert_fifth_problem`: Hilbert's fifth problem, solved by Gleason, Montgomery and Zippin.

## Implementation notes

`AdmitsLieGroupStructure G`, defined in
`FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Geometry.Manifold.LieGroupPresentation`, says that `G` is
continuously isomorphic to a finite-dimensional real-analytic Lie group. Lie groups are Hausdorff
but not assumed second countable: every discrete group is a `0`-dimensional Lie group
(`admitsLieGroupStructure_of_discreteTopology`). This matters for the Hilbert–Smith conjecture,
since uncountable discrete groups act continuously and faithfully on connected manifolds, for
instance `ℝ` with the discrete topology acting on `ℝ` by translations.

The acting group is not assumed Hausdorff: a topological group acting continuously and
faithfully on a Hausdorff space is Hausdorff, because the closure of the identity acts trivially.

The hypotheses on the manifold `X` are written in each theorem. A section variable
`[ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]` is included only in a theorem that mentions `n`,
so it would be dropped silently from a statement that mentions only `X`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
- [Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
- [Pardon 2013] J. Pardon, *The Hilbert–Smith conjecture for three-manifolds*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 26 (2013), 879–899. https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-2013-00766-3,
  [arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)
- [Myers–Steenrod 1939] S. B. Myers, N. E. Steenrod, *The group of isometries of a Riemannian
  manifold*, Ann. of Math. 40 (1939), 400–416. https://doi.org/10.2307/1968928
- [van den Dries–Goldbring 2015] L. van den Dries, I. Goldbring, *Hilbert's 5th problem*,
  Enseign. Math. 61 (2015), 3–43. https://doi.org/10.4171/LEM/61-1/2-2
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Hilbert5

open scoped Manifold ContDiff Bundle

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] {n : ℕ}

/-- The circle group admits a Lie group structure. -/
@[category test, AMS 22]
theorem admitsLieGroupStructure_circle : AdmitsLieGroupStructure Circle :=
  admitsLieGroupStructure_of_lieGroup (n := 1)

/-- The discrete group `ℤ` admits a Lie group structure. -/
@[category test, AMS 22]
theorem admitsLieGroupStructure_multiplicative_int :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
  admitsLieGroupStructure_of_discreteTopology

/-- **Hilbert–Smith conjecture**: every locally compact topological group acting continuously
and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. -/
@[category research open, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- The Hilbert–Smith conjecture holds for actions by isometries of a connected smooth Riemannian
manifold `X`: the isometry group of `X` is a Lie group by the Myers–Steenrod theorem, so `G` has
no small subgroups and is a Lie group by the Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin theorem.

Here `X` carries its Riemannian distance (`IsRiemannianManifold`), so the metric topology of `X`
is its manifold topology. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 53 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    [ConnectedSpace X] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ X]
    [Bundle.RiemannianBundle (fun x : X ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle (𝓡 n) ∞ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (fun x : X ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold (𝓡 n) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X]
    (hiso : ∀ g : G, Isometry (g • · : X → X)) :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- **Pardon's theorem** (2013): the Hilbert–Smith conjecture holds for connected 3-manifolds,
see [Pardon 2013]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- **p-adic formulation**: the p-adic integers `ℤ_[p]` cannot act continuously and faithfully
on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold. This is equivalent to
`hilbert_smith_conjecture` by the Gleason–Yamabe theorem together with Newman's theorem on
periodic transformations of manifolds. -/
@[category research open, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_padic_formulation {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [AddAction ℤ_[p] X] [ContinuousVAdd ℤ_[p] X] :
    ¬ FaithfulVAdd ℤ_[p] X := by
  sorry

/-- **Hilbert's fifth problem** (Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin, 1952): every Hausdorff topological
group modeled on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space is continuously isomorphic to a real-analytic
Lie group.

The input `ChartedSpace` supplies only a topological atlas. The compatible analytic atlas and
analytic group operations belong to the output `LieGroupPresentation`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 57]
theorem hilbert_fifth_problem
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G] :
    Nonempty (LieGroupPresentation G n) := by
  sorry

end Hilbert5

reformulations.difference: The Lean manifold X is only a Hausdorff, connected space with a topological atlas on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`; it is not assumed second countable or paracompact. The acting group G is not assumed Hausdorff. The conclusion `AdmitsLieGroupStructure G` asks for a topological-group isomorphism (`≃ₜ*`) onto an analytic (`ω`) Lie group, which need not be second countable. Textbook conventions often assume second-countable manifolds and smooth Lie groups.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) G is automatically Hausdorff. If g and h are inseparable, then g•x and h•x are inseparable for every x, so they are equal because X is T2. Faithfulness then gives g = h, so G is T0, and a T0 topological group is T2. I proved this in Lean in the scratch file. (2) Lie groups must not be required to be second countable. Otherwise the statement would be false: ℝ with the discrete topology acts continuously and faithfully on ℝ by translations. Tao states this convention explicitly ('I am not requiring manifolds (or Lie groups) here to be second countable'). A locally compact NSS group, in Yamabe's sense of a Lie group, carries a compatible analytic Lie structure: its identity component is an open Lie subgroup, and charts are transported by translation. So 'analytic' costs nothing. (3) Allowing non-second-countable X does not change the conjecture. The standard reduction to ℤ_p (Tao's §3, via Gleason–Yamabe, Peter–Weyl and Newman's theorems) is local. It only applies the ℤ_p case and Newman's theorem to invariant open sets G'B and GB, which are σ-compact, hence second countable, n-manifolds. It uses connectedness of X only at the last step. Pardon: 'For any specific manifold M, Conjectures 1.1–1.3 for M are equivalent' and 'The approach is local on M'. So the conjecture over arbitrary Hausdorff connected n-manifolds is equivalent to the second-countable version. (4) A jointly continuous faithful action (`ContinuousSMul` + `FaithfulSMul`) is equivalent to Pardon's 'continuous injection G → Homeo(M) with the compact-open topology', because M is locally compact Hausdorff.

reformulations.difference: The source says ℤ_p cannot act continuously and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional manifold. The Lean states `¬ FaithfulVAdd ℤ_[p] X` for every continuous additive action on any Hausdorff connected space X with an atlas on ℝⁿ; X is not assumed second countable.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `¬ FaithfulVAdd` means some a ≠ 0 acts trivially, i.e. the action is not faithful. To reduce a non-second-countable X to a second-countable one, suppose ℤ_p acts faithfully on X. The kernel of the action on any invariant set is a closed subgroup, so it is 0 or p^kℤ_p. Hence for each k some element of p^kℤ_p moves some point x_k. Join the x_k to x_0 by paths (X is path connected), and cover the paths by countably many chart balls. This gives a connected, σ-compact open set U containing x_0 and all x_k. Choose m with p^mℤ_p + x_0 ⊆ U, and set V = p^mℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p. Then V+U is open, connected (each a+U meets U), σ-compact (image of V×U), hence second countable, and V-invariant. V acts faithfully on V+U, since for k ≥ m some element of p^kℤ_p ⊆ V moves x_k. The converse direction is trivial.

reformulations.difference: G is not assumed second countable. The Lie group presentation is required to have exactly the dimension n of the atlas. The `T2Space G` hypothesis is redundant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A locally Euclidean space is T1, and a T1 topological group is T2, so `T2Space` adds nothing. The dimension n is forced by invariance of domain. Non-second-countable G reduces to the classical case: the identity component G₀ is open (G is locally connected) and σ-compact (it is generated by a compact neighbourhood), hence second countable. Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin makes G₀ an analytic Lie group. Conjugations are continuous, hence analytic, automorphisms of G₀. Charts on cosets by translation make G an analytic n-dimensional Lie group. This matches Tao's Theorem 1 ('a topological group which is locally Euclidean ... is isomorphic to a Lie group'), with Tao's stated non-second-countable convention.

review.notes:
I found no misformalizations and no stale statuses.

- Status: the Hilbert–Smith conjecture and its ℤ_p form are still open. Wikipedia, Pardon's paper and arXiv listings show no accepted resolution beyond Pardon's 3-dimensional case. Pardon's theorem (n = 3), the isometric case (Myers–Steenrod plus NSS ⇒ Lie) and Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin are correctly tagged solved.
- Lean checks in /workspace/review:
  1. The fiber norm and inner product in the Riemannian variant's `IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle` hypothesis come from the `RiemannianBundle` metric, not from a flat Euclidean instance.
  2. The Riemannian variant's hypotheses are satisfiable, with X = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
  3. The main conjecture's hypotheses are satisfiable, with Circle acting on itself.
  4. `ω` means analytic (`contDiff_omega_iff_analyticOnNhd`), so `LieGroupPresentation` is a genuine Lie group and `hilbert_fifth_problem` is not trivial.
  5. The implementation note's claim that a topological group acting continuously and faithfully on a T2 space is T2 is proved in Lean.
- The conclusion `AdmitsLieGroupStructure` is not trivially true: ℤ_p is not homeomorphic to any topological manifold.
- The non-second-countable convention for Lie groups is needed: ℝ with the discrete topology acting on ℝ would otherwise refute the conjecture. Tao states this convention explicitly.
- The references (Pardon JAMS 26 (2013) 879–899; Myers–Steenrod Ann. Math. 40 (1939) 400–416; van den Dries–Goldbring Enseign. Math. 61, 3–43) match Crossref.
